small_guidance:
- The softmax/sigmoid epilogue is already cheap; the runtime is dominated by `nn.ConvTranspose3d`. Tuning BLOCK_S of the epilogue further will not move `fast_p` meaningfully — focus must shift to the conv-transpose itself.
- If keeping the current epilogue, fuse it directly with the bias add of the conv-transpose (drop bias=True from torch op, pass bias into the Triton kernel) to remove one full read/write pass over the (N, 64, 32, 64, 64) tensor.
- Try a single-pass channelwise softmax: with C=64 and BLOCK_C=64, set BLOCK_S=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=2, and keep the row resident in registers — the current 2D tile already does this, so the win is small.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add (or input-stationary gather) kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), computing `output[n, oc, od, oh, ow] = Σ_{ic,kd,kh,kw} x[n, ic, id, ih, iw] * w[ic, oc, kd, kh, kw]` with the standard ConvT index math `id*stride + kd - pad = od` solved for valid (id,kd) pairs. The conv dominates ~10ms of runtime and is the only place with real headroom.
- Fuse the entire epilogue (bias add + channel softmax + sigmoid) into the conv-transpose kernel's store path: have the conv kernel produce a full (C=64) channel column for one spatial location per program, then reduce-max / exp / sum / divide / sigmoid in registers before storing. With OC=64 fitting in a single tile, the softmax reduction is free.
- Use channels_last_3d layout so the OC axis is contiguous; tile (BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SPATIAL=32 or 64) with BLOCK_K over `IC*KD*KH*KW`=864 in chunks of 32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2 — well within the 132 KB SMEM budget on the 4090.
